LanguageData.TSA_WD_Raid_GarrisonRetainTooltip: Settlements and outposts always keep at least this percentage of their maximum strength at home when sending a raid, trader caravan, or building crew (roads, roadblocks, spike traps, fortify). Tier max for settlements, occupant max for outposts. Decontamination crews are exempt. Primary attackers and allies use the same rule for raids.

LanguageData.TSA_WD_Raid_TravelPrepExactPct: Pre-raid exact path and travel cost calculation
LanguageData.TSA_WD_Raid_TravelPrepExactPctTip: Share of raid/trader destination prep assessments that use full world pathfinding (FindPath). 0% always uses the crow-flies heuristic (often the biggest performance gain on huge worlds). 100% always pathfinds. In between, a deterministic cadence uses exact pathing that share of the time. Prep can understate mountain/sea detours (e.g. real path 4× longer), so a raid may launch that arrives weaker: acceptable fog of war, not a bug. Launch still uses a real path. Also managed by Setting presets → Performance when you use those packs.
LanguageData.TSA_WD_Raid_LossPerHourTooltip: The percentage of current strength lost every hour during travel. The longer a raid force is on the road, the more strength they lose.
LanguageData.TSA_WD_Raid_MaxTravelDaysTooltip: The hard limit for how long a WD Traveler (Raid, Expansion, Road Building Caravan) can remain in the field. If a caravan reaches this limit before hitting its target, the mission is aborted and the force is lost.
LanguageData.TSA_WD_Raid_DropPodChanceT3Tip: When a tier-3 settlement launches a raid and meets the tech gate, this is the chance it uses ballistic drop pods instead of a walking caravan. Same attrition formula as T4 drop pods.
LanguageData.TSA_WD_Raid_DropPodChanceTip: When a tier-4 settlement launches a raid and meets the tech gate, this is the chance it uses ballistic drop pods instead of a walking caravan. Launch gate, letter, and arrival strength all use the same drop-pod attrition formula.
LanguageData.TSA_WD_Raid_DropPodMinTechTip: Only factions at this tech level or higher may launch drop-pod raids. Neolithic allows essentially all factions.
LanguageData.TSA_WD_Raid_DropPodAttritionMultTip: Multiplies strength loss per hour for drop-pod raids. Attrition uses crow-flies distance (ignore terrain) and is applied at launch so gate, letter, and traveler strength match.
LanguageData.TSA_WD_Raid_ColonySiegeChanceTip: When a normal (walking) raid caravan from a T3 or T4 settlement arrives at your colony, chance the map raid uses the Siege strategy. Drop-pod raids never roll siege.
LanguageData.TSA_WD_Raid_MinRatioTooltip: Minimum strength advantage required for an NPC to consider a raid on an outpost or NPC settlement viable. Raids on your colony use a separate storyteller-points gate: attackers need at least 0.7× those points, then −0.1× per quiet day (floor 0). Quiet means days since the colony was last picked as a WD raid target. When a settlement would raid the colony, the nearest same-faction settlement that still passes that gate launches instead.
LanguageData.TSA_WD_Raid_RazeChanceTooltip: Chance that a successful automatic NPC raid razes the target instead of founding a conqueror settlement. Razed tiles leave timed ruins that block new settlements and outposts nearby until they clear.
LanguageData.TSA_WD_Raid_RuinLingerDaysTooltip: How long WD settlement ruins remain on the map after a raze. They use the same neighbor blocking distance as settlements and outposts, then despawn.
LanguageData.TSA_WD_Raid_TargetRadTooltip: Max distance (in tiles) a settlement will look to find a target.
